Topic: Change of Basis: Seeing the World Through Different Eyes

Target audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

Section: section_1 — Introduction: The Perspective Problem

Lecture lines:
One point can have many different coordinate descriptions.
An explorer uses a standard North-East grid.
A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid.
They see the same "X" using different numbers.
Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis.

Planned animations:
Draw a standard white (#FFFFFF) grid with a red 'X' (#FF0000) at (3, 2).
Introduce character 'Explorer' on the left side associated with the standard grid.
Overlay a tilted and stretched yellow (#FFFF00) grid representing the 'Pirate's' map.
Highlight the red 'X' (#FF0000) position relative to the Pirate's yellow grid lines.
Add labels: Standard [3, 2] in white (#FFFFFF) and Pirate [v1, v2] in yellow (#FFFF00).

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Vector

Lecture lines:
A vector is a recipe of basis vectors.
Vector [3, 2] means 3 i-steps and 2 j-steps.
We reach the target by scaling and adding arrows.

Planned animations:
Draw standard unit vectors i (blue, #0000FF) and j (green, #00FF00) at the origin.
Animate a robot icon moving 3 units along i, then 2 units along j.
Draw the resulting vector [3, 2] from origin to the robot's position in purple (#800080).

Section: section_3 — Visualizing a New Basis

Lecture lines:
Let's define a new basis using vectors b1 and b2.
These vectors form a squashed and rotated grid.
The space remains fixed while our ruler changes.

Planned animations:
Show a dim grey (#696969) standard grid in the background.
Introduce basis vectors b1 (orange, #FFA500) and b2 (cyan, #00FFFF) starting from origin.
Generate a new skewed grid using orange (#FFA500) and cyan (#00FFFF) lines.

Section: section_4 — The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix

Lecture lines:
Matrix P bridges these two different coordinate worlds.
Its columns are new basis vectors in standard terms.
This matrix serves as a translation manual between grids.

Planned animations:
Display standard basis vectors i (#0000FF) and j (#00FF00) as reference.
Plot Pirate's basis vectors b1 (#FFA500) at [2, 1] and b2 (#00FFFF) at [-1, 1].
Highlight the standard coordinates of b1 and b2 with dashed lines.
Form matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]] by placing b1 and b2 as columns.
Label the columns of P as 'b1' and 'b2' in their respective colors.

Section: section_5 — The Mathematical Transformation

Lecture lines:
We translate new coordinates using matrix multiplication.
Matrix P converts pirate coordinates to standard ones.
P-inverse performs the reverse translation back to the pirate.
The formula [v]_standard equals P times [v]_new.
This math keeps everyone's perspective perfectly aligned.

Planned animations:
Display formula [v]_std = P * [v]_new in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Show the Pirate's vector [1, 1] in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the formula.
Substitute matrix P and vector [1, 1] into the matrix multiplication.
Calculate the product: [2*1 + -1*1, 1*1 + 1*1] resulting in [1, 2].
Highlight the resulting vector [1, 2] on the standard grid in white (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_6 — Summary & Global View

Lecture lines:
Change of basis maps grids to different perspectives.
It is the foundation for diagonalization and compression.
One vector, many views: that is change of basis.

Planned animations:
Display a sequence: Basis -> Grid -> Matrix -> Translation in white (#FFFFFF).
Morph the tilted grid back to standard while the vector arrow remains fixed.
Display 'Diagonalization' and 'Compression' as key applications in green (#00FF00).
